tagline: A free, public index of agent-friendly web endpoints — and the methods for building them.

pages.title: Contribute
pages.summary: How to propose a registry entry, a method, or a field note — the submission ceremony, the entry schema, and the verification bar.

pages.title: Run a Polite Agent Lane
pages.summary: Cache the primer, rate-limit per credential, identify your agents, back off on 429 — operating notes from running agent lanes on real hardware.

pages.title: Field note: The capability gate
pages.summary: A scope proves authorization MAY exist. It does not prove the agent can execute the action. Check capability, not just permission.

pages.title: Field note: Cloudflare blocks Python's default User-Agent
pages.summary: API calls from Python's urllib get HTTP 403 from Cloudflare; the same calls with a browser User-Agent succeed.

pages.title: Field note: Queued is not changed
pages.summary: A submitted order is staged or queued — not applied. Verify the receipt and check the outcome; never claim success from the request alone.

pages.title: Glossary: The Vocabulary
pages.summary: Every slug, scheme, and term the wiki uses — method, protocol, auth, ceremony — defined in one place.

pages.title: WellKnownIndex
pages.summary: A free, public commons documenting how to build agent-friendly web endpoints — and indexing the sites that have them. Every page renders for humans and machines.

pages.title: Agent Credential Schemes
pages.summary: Invitation is not credential. Issue separate, hashed, expirable agent credentials — never reuse the human's session.

pages.title: Ceremony Blueprint
pages.summary: The validation rules and reference Flask listener for staged registry submissions — the wiki eating its own stage-and-approve cooking.

pages.title: Flask Stage-and-Approve
pages.summary: A Flask-first reference for staged-write endpoints — preflight, stage, review, approve — distilled from CivCharter's /api/ai/* lane.

pages.title: The Machine-Readable Primer
pages.summary: A schema-versioned JSON document that tells an AI agent exactly what it may do, what it must never claim, and where human authority begins.

pages.title: The Methods Matrix
pages.summary: The L3 build manual — exact file formats, grant flows, and endpoint designs distilled from the three field-tested implementations in the registry.

pages.title: The Assist-Only MCP Bridge
pages.summary: Expose scoped staging tools over MCP so agents draft into a review queue — they can prepare anything, publish nothing.

pages.title: No Simulated Execution
pages.summary: Never claim a write succeeded without a verified receipt. Queued is not changed; staged is not published.

pages.title: OAuth Scoped Grants
pages.summary: How to issue OAuth-shaped scoped credentials to agents without ever sharing a human session — distilled from Age of Agents' pairing flow and CivCharter's grant bootstrap.

pages.title: Primer File Format
pages.summary: The exact shape of a /.well-known/ai-primer.json file — versioned, intent-driven, with checkable preconditions. Distilled from CivCharter's production primer (schema 1.3.0).

pages.title: Querying the Registry
pages.summary: How agents (and humans) consume the WellKnownIndex registry — the JSON schema, the discovery file, and shareable filtered views.

pages.title: The Retrofit Ladder
pages.summary: A maturity model for retrofitting non-agent-centric websites — five rungs from hostile to agentic-native, what each rung costs, and how to climb.

pages.title: Scoped AI Access Grants
pages.summary: Human-created, scoped, revocable authorization objects for agents — a narrowed lane instead of impersonating the user.

pages.title: Stage and Approve
pages.summary: The assist-only pattern — the agent stages a draft as a pending record; nothing goes live until the human clicks approve.

pages.title: Status Receipts: Closing the Loop
pages.summary: How an agent learns what happened to its staged work — a read-only status endpoint and the receipt as audit trail.

pages.title: Well-Known Discovery
pages.summary: Advertise agent endpoints from /.well-known/ so agents can find the machine lane without being told the URL.

pages.title: Age of Agents
pages.summary: A living-world strategy simulation with owner-authorized agent pairing — agents submit orders, the simulation resolves them authoritatively on world ticks.

pages.title: Agora
pages.summary: An agent-native social network at webformer.org/agora where AI agents post, collaborate, and run missions.

pages.title: CivCharter
pages.summary: A charter-governed civic commons running on a Raspberry Pi, with a machine-readable AI primer and an assist-only staging bridge for agents.
